utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we start with the hearing, there's just one little housekeeping matter. There is a request, I think, from the interpreters that we read the following message to all participants in court. The message reads: "Since the instalment of the new audio equipment in the courtrooms, interpreters have been experiencing problems with the quality of the sound which is in turn affecting the quality of interpretation. Speakers who stand are less audible than before, and even the slightest incidental noise is picked up. Court reporters, too, are experiencing similar problems with the new equipment. Until a solution is found to remedy the situation, all participants in the proceedings are kindly requested to do the following: One, make sure they speak directly into the microphone; keep the lectern and/or papers away from the microphone; switch off the microphone as soon as they stop speaking; to the extent possible, keep all typing to a minimum; avoid shuffling papers, clicking pens, et cetera. Technicians are kindly requested to switch off any microphones inadvertently left open." And you have been thanked for your understanding. Could we kindly observe the request from the interpreters to make their job a little more bearable. Mr. Grujic. Am I right? May I remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Grujic. We will now continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to try to speak directly to your mike, Mr. Milovancevic, and try to speak a little louder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: From May 1993, Mr. Grujic, when you were appointed president of the Commission for Imprisoned and Missing Persons of the Republic of Croatia to date, is it the case that you are dealing with imprisoned and missing persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can it be said that at that period you were heading all the bodies of the Republic of Croatia, whatever their name, that dealt with issues of imprisoned and missing persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Today you are heading the Commission for Imprisoned and Missing Persons in the Ministry for Family and Intergenerational Solidarity?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In point 4 of your report, the scope of this administration is specified under 2f. That's an addendum.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That scope is defined as technical matters related to search for detainees and missing persons, exhumation, and identification of mortal remains from individual and mass graves of persons killed in armed conflicts?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Was the definition of the activities of the Commission for Imprisoned and Missing Persons which you headed before defined in a similar way?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the decree about the internal -- decree on the internal structure that we mentioned before, it is said that the job of the administration is to gather, process, and keep records of persons kept in detention during the Homeland War.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's one of the purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you understand under the term "Homeland War" and what is understood under the term "enemy camps"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Homeland War is defined in the Republic of Croatia as the period -- I cannot give you exact dates, but between 1991 and 1995. And as for enemy camps and prisons, that term means the places of illegal detention where people were rounded up and taken away from the Republic of Croatia, and they were located in the former Republic of Yugoslavia, certain areas of Croatia and Bosnia, and formed a unified system of camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back in time a little. In chapter 6 of your report, you say that in end 1993, it was decided to renew requests to trace detainees and missing persons. Was that so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was decided to conduct in 1994 a renewal of requests for search for missing persons in order to arrive at an exact number of such persons at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As we learned from your report in paragraph 7, new questionnaires were developed and it was organised that they be filled in again in "Areas of the Republic of Croatia which at that time were not occupied." Can you explain what areas are that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the part of Croatia that was not occupied at the time. I don't think it's necessary to explain to you now which areas of Croatia were occupied and which were not. Suffice it to say that one-third of the territory of Croatia was occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean those parts of the territory of Croatia that were not covered by UNPAs, United Nations Protected Areas as defined by the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean those parts of Croatia over which the Republic of Croatia had no authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that on the occasion when these requests were renewed new questionnaires were developed. We have an example, a sample of this questionnaire as addendum 6a to your report. In paragraph 18 -- rather, in item 18 of the questionnaire, it is required to specify whether the person was a member of active or reserve forces of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, a member of the ZNG, an active or reserve policeman, a Home Corps Guard, or a member of civilian defence at the time of arrest.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think you have mentioned all the possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what is this term "domobran," which is one of the options, "home guard"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two categories that are possible. People who were part of labour units, something close to civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that there were two categories of Home Guards?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that there were two categories. It's the name of a specific military unit that was given that name at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can I infer then that when you say Home Guard you mean members of certain military units that are different from civilian defence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were certainly not civilian defence. Civilian defence is one category, and Home Guards are another category.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what you understand under "Member of civilian defence," because that is one of the group of -- groups of persons indicated in this question in the questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will allow that I am not a specialist on the establishment of various forces in Croatia. That is the way they were designated and enumerated at the time when these units and formations were established in Croatia and that's how we named them in the questionnaire. I cannot tell you what they were and how they were distinct from others. We just put them in the questionnaire as they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In this same questionnaire, in part II, which is entitled "Data on the forced removal, disappearance, or capture" of the person, you mention in item 8, "Question: Who forcibly removed or arrested the person." You give these possibilities. "A: Members of the units of JA; B: Members of the Territorial Defence of JA; C: Members of paramilitary units, police, from temporarily occupied areas of the Republic of Croatia; D: Members of other paramilitary units; E: Members of secret services; F: Civilians; G: Others. Is that correct yes.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you mention members of units of JA and members of Territorial Defence of JA, what do you mean and what does JA mean?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: JA means the then Yugoslav army and members of Territorial Defence. That is clear. That means Territorial Defence units that were under the authority of the then Yugoslav army but with the establishment of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the first part of this questionnaire, which is entitled "General details of the person sought," the following is listed, name, surname, maiden name, nickname, father's name, mother's name, date of birth, place of birth, municipality, town, parish or county, state, citizenship, ethnicity, and religion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And finally in part V, at the very end of the questionnaire under V we have general information about the requesting person, the person who is looking for the missing person and who signs the request has to give their Yugoslav identity number, name, surname, father's name, residence, street, town, municipality, UNPA area, citizenship, ethnicity, religion, and kinship with the person sought. Those are the details that the requesting person had to indicate.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or, rather, let me specify. It was not required that the requesting person give all these details. They could if they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You say in your report that on that occasion in connection with these renewed requests in the period from the 14th of February to the 5th of March, 1994, requests were renewed for a total of 35 -- 3.052 persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So at that time, was it the number of persons whose fate was unknown who had earlier been imprisoned or missing?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the end of that particular operation of ours, that was the final number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that for each of these persons a special dossier was established that contained all the other documentation in addition to the questionnaire concerning the said person?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That questionnaire was complete, and it contained the sum of all information about the missing person. If any other information about the missing person was available, a medical file or a document from the public domain, it was included in the dossier, but the questionnaire was the basis of the dossier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly as saying that based on this renewed requested for the search for a missing person that was done in 1994, requests were renewed for a total of 3.052 persons which means that questionnaires were filled for each and every one of them and dossiers were formed for each and one of them, that is there are 3.052 dossiers in existence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We will now move on to information about exhumed persons. That would be paragraph 31 of the report you provided. The collection and processing of information about exhumed persons was the responsibility of the administration that you headed. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 31 on the report, and we have a chart enclosed as well, it says that a total of 3.568 bodies were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me to which territory does this number pertain?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The territory that used to be occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that those are the territories that used to be UNPAs?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll put it this way. Those are the territories where the Republic of Croatia had no control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that one of the details that the requesting person had to indicate in the questionnaire was the specification of the particular UNPA where the person went missing?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the possible questions, and they were included in the questionnaire because the process of release and exchange of prisoners, as well as relations with commanders of certain zones were separated. So we covered different areas separately. It doesn't mean that the entire territory was under UNPAs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in noting that in item 5 of the questionnaire, under the title "Personal details of the requesting persons," one of the questions was "UNPA zone, sector"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If -- if applicable. If that person was in such an area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Since the territory of the then SAO Krajina was included in the UNPAs, do you have information that pertains to the SAO Krajina or the municipalities that comprised it as regards the exhumed persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that way, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: From the survey of the number of exhumed bodies according to counties, it is evident that most of the bodies, that is to say 1.969 out of a total of 3.568, were exhumed in the Vukovar-Srem district or county; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where this county is?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That county is on the east of the Republic of Croatia, and I think that it is very clearly depicted on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that Eastern Slavonia is outside the borders of the SAO Krajina that was included in the UNPAs?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that would be right. The current administrative border, the present-day administrative border -- well, we can talk about administrative borders nowadays that are in inside the Republic of Croatia and as such these borders exist. This survey shows that in the territory of that count ill the largest number of mortal remains was found. Territorially speaking, most of that county was occupied but not entirely. For example, the town of Vinkovci was not occupied but it belongs to that county. So the counties were administratively set up, and they still exist to this day, and that's the only thing that we can talk about. It is clear that in that county, although it was not fully occupied, most of the mortal remains had been found this their but in the territory that had been occupied, which can be proven.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When UNPAs were established, through Security Council Resolutions of the United Nations, these zones were divided according to municipalities which then in 1991 existed in the territory of Croatia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not talk about that. I do not have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You gave a survey of exhumed persons here in a way that includes a new territorial division of the Republic of Croatia which is different from that territorial division according to municipalities that existed in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. In 1991, the territorial division was different. This is a division which is in force now and that was in force at the moment when we started the process of exhumations. We cannot go back now. And if we start the process in 1996, we cannot go back to the division of the state that existed in 1991. That would be absurd.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to indicate something else to you, that these proceedings are taking place in relation to a particular territory, and the description of the area where something is going on pertains to the municipal divisions that existed in 1991 in the territory of Croatia. What you said to us just now, does that indicate that you cannot give an answer concerning the number of exhumed persons in the territories or municipalities that existed in Croatia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I cannot give know that and I cannot say that, but we know about the actual sites, the actual places where the exhumations were carried out, and we're talking about the exhumations that have to do with this indictment. We talk about individual sites. And I cannot talk about other sites. I cannot talk about other place. I cannot talk about other territorial divisions if the process of exhumations started in 1996.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Milovancevic please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, the interpreter asks you to please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In your report that pertains to exhumations, you say that 2.982 exhumed bodies were identified. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I can see, 72 per cent of the identified persons are men. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Also, almost 60 per cent of the identified persons are between the ages of 18 and 60. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 39 per cent is over 60 -- are over 60, and 50 per cent are between the ages of 18 and 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the graph that pertains to these exhumations, it says that 111 persons are of an unknown age; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain this to us? How can a person be identified without knowing his or her age?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, especially in the case of the elderly, because documents in their places of residence were destroyed. They were in the occupied territories. And according to the statements of their relatives, there would be a difference. One relative would say the person was born in 1907. Another person would give another year. Or perhaps they can agree on the year but not the actual date. So this is a small number of persons whose exact date of birth cannot be established, and that is why it says "Age unknown." That is precisely why we operated this way. We wanted to stand firmly by every name that we gave, and when we cannot do that we say "Unknown."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Would it be more accurate to say in the case of such cases at least what their year of birth was even if you don't know the actual date?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but then you would ask me, "Why did you not give a date?" Our position was that in those cases where we cannot give firm, accurate information about a particular person, that person was in the category of unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Among these 3.052 exhumed persons that were identified, there is also 142 Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we are going to deal with a chapter of your report that relates to information about persons who were killed. That is 34 in your statement. So I would like to ask you the following: In 34b which was displayed on graph 7 or chart 7, it says that 12.078 persons were killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said in my statement, it is the least possible number, because that is the number of persons who were killed that we have identified until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, you head the agency for detained and missing persons.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that information about killed persons does not come from your office?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's wrong. In the year 2000, the government of the Republic of Croatia passed a decree authorising my office and myself to compile a single list of killed persons for the needs of The Hague Tribunal, for the trials that were taking place then and that are still ongoing. I compiled such a list, and in my introductory remarks I said that I used certain sources. I said what sources I used, what lists I used in order to make a single list, that is to say a list of the Ministry of Defence, lists of the Ministry of Health, then the Crisis Staff. All these lists were brought into one. They were all compiled in order to establish this single list of persons killed, and that is at least 12.000, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In your report that pertains to these persons who were killed, you said that the source of that information about killed persons is the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Family and Other Matters, and Veterans, and the statistics office; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the methods that these organs used when compiling information about killed persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know. The Ministry of Health received information from hospitals and from the ground, and this information was set up in a systematic manner, and that is how they compiled their records. Of course the Ministry of Defence, too, had information about all members of the armed forces. When a person would get killed, his unit would send this information on. So all this information would be centralised and a list would be compiled. Since we had these two lists in the Ministry of Defence -- but lest there be any confusion, you mentioned the ministry of defenders, but some information was sent there too. So it's the same information but because of this new set-up of Ministries the ministry of defenders included this information, veterans, but it's the same information basically. But I, in my office, have all the lists brought under a single umbrella. This is clear information. This is a clear-cut list. And in all those lists where we did not have enough elements, where we could not be sure that there weren't any mistakes, those things were simply deleted if we did not have enough particulars to be included in a list for The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that you got lists of persons from these different institutions. I'm interested in the following: Did you have before you or did you have insight into materials under which this information is based?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we had that. This wasn't done in the course of one day. It was a long process that involved teams consisting of people from these institutions and from my institution. So every piece of information was checked and double checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which territory and which time period is relevant for this list of killed persons, of 12.078 persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said up to 1995. From when up to 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean from when?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What is the beginning of this period concerning these killed persons? That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but it's from 1991, the beginning of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly, and can I say on the basis of what you said that this number of killed persons of 12.078 persons involves a list of killed persons who were killed from the beginning of 1991 until 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. So it does not include the military operations of Flash and Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Witness, that's not what I asked you. I did not ask you about that operation. My next question is: Does this report mean that we do not have the number of persons killed in 1995, for all of 1995? That is to say from the 1st of January, 1995, onwards? We don't have that information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Just a moment. Let us put things properly. This number includes all persons who were killed and who were possible to identify until the end of the military police operation Storm. So it covers the entire area of the Homeland War over which my office is competent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you were first answering my question to which period this figure 12.078 killed persons relates, you said until 1995.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say which month in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: To my subsequent question, you said -- can you tell us now until which month is the report valid?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can say that it's until June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does this answer mean that this list of 12.078 killed persons includes every person killed until May 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not so cut and dried. We have to explain this in broader terms. The way in which you are formulating your questions cannot produce the correct answer to the question. These 12.078 persons were killed in connection with the aggression on the Republic of Croatia. In addition to that, but your questions didn't cover this area, we have persons killed during military operations Flash and Storm, most of whom have not been identified and properly buried yet. So we could not include them in lists because they are not connected to identities yet. So this list is subject to updating, constant updating. Exhumations are going on. We have people killed in the Republic of Croatia and people killed during military operations Flash and Storm, and all of them are being added to appropriate lists. Up to this moment, we have this number on record, and of course with every new identification of any category of death these lists will be updated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is me or the way I'm formulating my questions, as you suggest, or the subject of your numbers. You said it was a list of persons killed until 1995. When I asked you again, you said it was a list of persons killed excluding those killed in Flash and Storm operations. You also said that persons killed in operations Flash and Storm did die, but they were not identified. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I'll try again. All persons who were killed from the beginning until the end of all armed conflicts in the Republic of Croatia, whether they were killed in 1991 or 1995 and maybe even beginning 1996, are on those lists. However, we have one category of persons who were killed in military police actions Flash and Storm and who were not identified. We know where they are buried. The process of their exhumation and the process of revealing new mass graves is ongoing. So we don't know when we start an exhumation whether the person was killed in 1991, 1992, or 1995, until identification is completed. Therefore, your question whether persons were recorded relative to a certain period is impossible. Why? Because I don't know whether this year I will find a new grave site containing bodies of people killed in, I don't know, 1991, 1992, or 1995. It can be anybody. The next person we identify can be somebody killed in October 1995. At this moment, I don't know the last date of the last death. You understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber doesn't. Is it possible from what you're telling us that in the number 12.078 are included people who were killed during Operations Flash and Storm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they were identified, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now do you determine after exhuming a body that this person died during Operation Storm and not during the previous war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all persons or almost all persons who were killed during military police operations Flash and Storm were buried according to Geneva Conventions in known sites, and in the process of exhuming these graves and for the purpose of identifying these persons and giving them a proper burial this is an ongoing process. So we know when these persons were killed and forensic experts can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you also know where they are buried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. We know where they were buried. Those lists were published and made available to the international community. I personally produced them to the representatives of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the course of discussions on humanitarian issues. Dossiers complete with pictures were also made available to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the international community, but also the ICTY either at the request of the ICTY or otherwise. The ICTY acts as a monitor in the process of these exhumations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Therefore, you are able to distinguish between bodies exhumed who were killed during Operation Storm and those who were killed in the other war, the previous war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you tell us of the 12.078 who were killed during Operation Storm and Flash, on the one hand, and the number that was killed in the previous war? I'm sorry, Mr. Milovancevic. I just want to get clarity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will now give you the information. 332 persons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 332 were identified in the course of such exhumations that were conducted upon request of the ICTY or together with representatives of the ICTY, or the ICTY was a monitor in such exhumations. So 332 persons from that period were identified, and they are on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I still don't understand you. My question to you is: Who or what number out of 12.078 were exhumed from graves resulting from Operations Flash and Storm, and what number were exhumed from the previous war, not ICTY. Just tell me which ones come from Operation Storm and which once come from the previous war. MR. MILOVANCEVIC? [Interpretation] I'm sorry to interrupt you. It seems that we are in closed session or in private session. Are we? Because it should be public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: According to my monitor we are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much. I'm sorry. I thought for a moment we were in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's okay, Mr. Milovancevic. Did you understand my question, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood, Your Honour. 332 persons were exhumed or identified from Operations Flash and Storm, 332.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the remainder from 12.078 were assumed died in the previous war? This is by logical deduction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic. Once again, I'm sorry to interrupt your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is completely in accordance with the rules. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you were responding to the Honourable Judge's question a moment ago, you said 332 persons were identified as persons killed during Operations Flash and Storm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I asked you the first time a question regarding these 12.078 persons killed, and the question was to which period this number relates, you said that those were persons killed until 1995. After that, you broadened your answer, saying it was until June 1995. Operation Storm was in August 1995, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but Flash was earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you were explaining about the period of time when these persons were killed, you said the report covers persons who were killed during the aggression against the republic of Croatia, and that is why persons killed during Flash and Storm were not included. Now responding to the Honourable Judge's question you said those persons were included after all. Which of the two is correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to -- I have to repeat. Records are kept in the following way: At the moment when we managed to identify any citizen of the Republic of Croatia regarding of -- regardless of their ethnicity, as soon as we get hold of an identifying document, at that moment that person is placed on the list of persons killed. Exhumations and identification of victims of Flash and Storm started relatively late, maybe a year ago or a year and a half ago, and in the course of regular updating they are progressively being included in the lists of persons killed. I cannot tell you exactly when any of them were identified and included in the lists. All I can tell you is 332 is the number currently for people killed during Flash and Storm in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you were answering Judge Moloto's question about the number of persons identified as having been killed in Flash and Storm operations, you said there were 332. Can you give me any information about their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. When we talk about persons killed, the number 12.078 includes 88.4 per cent Croats and 3.82 per cent Serbs, or in numbers - we are talking about cases where ethnicity is known - 7.012 persons of Croat ethnicity, 302 persons of Serb ethnicity, 195 who had declared themselves as Yugoslavs, and 402 other ethnicities. So we're talking only about those whose ethnicity's known. 7.400 or 500. I could add them up if you want me to. Whereas the ethnicity of the rest is not known.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you stated the percentage of persons killed who were Croats, you gave us a number different from the one shown in diagram number 6, where it says that 89 per cent of those killed were Croats?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must forgive me. That was based on an old figure, 11.834. I will give you the latest number in a second. 12.078 is the total, and the percentage is 88.4 -- or, rather, 80.76.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure you understood me. What I mean is this addendum 6 in the chapter related to persons killed, the big pie chart, it has 89 per cent and a total of 7.012 persons of Croat ethnicity killed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you say again which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That is the chart that is marked as "ethnicity of killed persons, persons," II. And then underneath it says "Analysis of those who are known, 7.911." So 89 per cent of those who are known were Croats. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave an explanation to the effect that the number of killed persons in Flash and Storm was included in the list of kid persons who were identified; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that this number is 332 and that out of them 302 persons were of Serb ethnicity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the diagram that you attached to this chapter about the number of killed persons, that is a chart entitled "Ethnicity of killed persons (III)," and the part that says "Others," that's 899 persons. You gave a diagram of all these others, including Bosniaks, Albanians, et cetera, not to go into all of that. There's certainly 20 ethnic groups or so. It says there were 302 Serbs. So I'm asking you whether this chart pertains to the ethnicity of killed persons that has to do with your entire report that is to say from 1991 to 1995, or is this just a chart that pertains to operations Flash and Storm?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This pertains to all of it. It was stated that 302 persons were of Serb ethnicity, that 195 persons were Yugoslavs. So it can be said that most were Serbs, but let's leave that aside. 302 persons stated that they were Serbs, which is not to say that all the persons who were found and identified in Operation Flash and Storm had declared themselves as ethnic Serbs. Perhaps they had not declared themselves at all. That is no one's obligation. No one is duty-bound to state his or her ethnicity. I could have provided ethnic background only for persons who actually said what their ethnicity was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, what you said just now, does that mean that from the beginning of 1991 until Operations Flash and Storm in the territory of Croat that not a single Serb got killed, that only 302 were killed in operations Flash and Storm is that what you're trying to tell us? Until then there were no casualties? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said, and that's not the way we can put it. I said that out of the shown persons that were identified, all of these persons who declared their ethnic background, we have the structure that I provided. That does not mean that among the rest, almost 5.000, there aren't any ethnic Serbs. On the contrary. I think there are ethnic Serbs there. So I can only talk about the information provided by the family during identification. If they did not want to state what their ethnicity was, but I mean 5.000 people did not. They did not say what their ethnic background was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you carried out exhumations of persons who were killed in Flash and Storm and that identifications are under way now. Can you tell me how many persons were exhumed in the territory of Croatia in relation to these two operations?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to these two operations, so far 499 persons were exhumed in Knin, Gracac, Korenica, and Zvanusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that in other places other victims were not found from these operations?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not what it means. I said already that there are burial sites that are known pertaining to Operations Flash and Storm, and that the international community was informed about these grave sites but also the representatives of Serbia and Montenegro, exclusively for humanitarian reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to get clarity, when you say Mr. Grujic in relation to these two operations, so far 499 persons were exhumed in Knin, Gracac, Korenica, and Zvanusa, by "two operations" do you refer to Flash and Storm, or do you refer to Flash and Storm on the one hand and the previous war on the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like to say that it is 499 persons, not 4.000. It is 499 persons. And could you please repeat this question to me? I did not quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is: What do you mean by the two operations in which 499 persons have been exhumed? What are these two operations you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Flash and Storm. Those are the two operations, Flash and Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, Mr. Grujic, I have one more question. You said that as for the information about persons killed in these operations - we are going to round up this chapter now - you submitted this information to international factors and to the government of Yugoslavia. Can you tell us how many persons are still considered as missing or killed in respect of these two operations?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just say a few words about this? Could I just say something in order to clarify matters? Missing persons from Flash and Storm were recorded in different ways, and their number was totally unknown. In the year 2000, I personally took an initiative at the meeting with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia aimed at clarifying the matter, namely that they give jurisdiction over these persons to the Republic of Croatia and that all abuse of these figures be stopped. We received an agreement on this basis and it is being implemented now. On the basis of these questionnaires presented here, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia said that they acknowledge this as a relevant questionnaire, and together with the International Red Cross, and this was preceded by education in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, the information-gathering process began in Operations Flash and Storm with regard to persons who were killed in Operations Flash and Storm. The process is still an ongoing one. So far, 915 dossiers were compiled. Two weeks ago, the Croatian parliament was informed about this. So for the time being we have these 915 persons that can be considered missing. In addition to that, it is very important to say at this point in time in order to understand the complexity of this subject matter, that at a meeting with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia - I beg your pardon, Serbia and Montenegro. I do beg your pardon - an agreement was reached or, rather, a document was signed defining the question of missing persons, including persons missing from Operations Flash and Storm. It says there that in territorial terms in the Republic of Croatia about 2.400 persons went missing, out of which 915 persons have currently been identified as from the Operations Flash and Storm. So approximately about two weeks ago, these persons were placed absolutely under the jurisdiction of the Republic of Croatia in terms of the request for these persons. And in addition to that, Serbia and Montenegro are looking for about 500 persons in the territory of Croatia. So in relation to the armed conflicts in the territory of the Republic of Croatia, another 1.140 persons are missing as recorded by the office for missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this would be the right time to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. We'll take the break and come back at quarter to eleven. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, when you responded to a question from Judge Moloto as to how many people were exhumed in relation to Operations Flash and Storm, you gave us the number of 332, out of which 300 or so Serbs.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. I know you said this before break, Mr. Milovancevic. The witness actually didn't say that the 302 are part of the 322. He said they are part of the 12.078.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. My apologies to the Trial Chamber. It's my mistake. I wrote down the two numbers next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, if in putting my question I misstate something, please correct me. It is not my intention to deliberately mislead you. Did I understand correctly that among the exhumed bodies there were 302 bodies of Serbs? That's the number you gave.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a number saying the total number of ethnic Serbs relative to the total number of exhumed persons, which doesn't mean there aren't more of them, because as I said, we were able to analyse only part of the data, namely those cases when family members indicated ethnicity. So you have that table that I provided that gives the number of 12.078 persons. Out of 12.078, 7.012 were those that declared themselves as Croats, 302 declared themselves as Serbs, 195 had declared themselves as Yugoslavs, and 402 had declared themselves as members of other national minorities, which means that we were able to analyse the data only of those who had specified their ethnicity, which means that 5.000 didn't, and necessarily those 5.000 include some Serbs, but I cannot tell you how many. I can only tell you about the facts that I have at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I understand you correctly, Mr. Grujic? Since these figures about Flash and Storm operations were not directly mentioned in your expert report, we are hearing them for the first time. Is it correct that your office registered 499 persons related to these operations? Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- or, rather, no, no. Not registered. We have to be precise. We didn't register, we exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's what I meant, the number of exhumed persons that were recorded as a number of 499. Out of those 499 exhumed persons, have some been identified? And how many?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 332 have been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Out of those 332, how many are Serbs and how many are other ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information because that was not supposed to be the subject of my testimony. Those are the numbers that I have in my head and that are not related to my testimony. The information you have been asking me recently is something that is not connected to my planned testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Related to the number of victims, you told us recently that according to the information available to your office the number of missing persons for the period May, August until the end of the year related to these operations is 915 missing in those operations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At this moment, that is the number we have. And I have to note, to emphasise, that this number is not only available to the office that I head, but the International Red Cross has the same number and it's documented.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This number of 915 persons, does it include the number of 499 exhumed persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and it cannot, because one category is identified -- or, rather, possibly. Those who are not identified and have been exhumed, some of them may be regarded as missing. So one part of this number 499 may be part of the missing persons, but we'll know that at some point in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly by saying that the process of exhumation started after 1995 in areas of the former Republic of Serbian Krajina which were UNPAs?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That process began on the territory of the Republic of Croatia. I would not like to get involved in a discussion about territories in this way. That is the territory of the Republic of Croatia, and at the moment when it was possible for the authorities of Croatia to get there exhumations began, and that was in 1996. Exhumations began in 1996 in areas where the Republic of Croatia did not have access before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We are in 2006. Is the process of exhumations finished in that area?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not. It is not finished either with regard to people who were killed in the period from 1991 to 1995, that is before Flash and Storm operations or with regard to people who were killed during Flash and Storm operations. All this is part of the government's programme that is being implemented continuously, with the proviso that people who were killed during Flash and Storm operations were buried. Their graves are mostly known. They have been recorded, and the lists of those grave sites have been made available to the international community and to Serbia and Montenegro for humanitarian reasons. And we are continuing to explore and search for new grave sites containing bodies of people who were killed between 1991 and 1995, that is before the beginning of Operations Flash and Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In response to one of the questions today, you explained that out of the 2.400 persons covered by the agreement between -- that 2.400 persons are covered by an agreement between Croatia on the one hand and Serbia and Montenegro on the other.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. What about them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said there was an agreement between Croatia and Serbia and Montenegro that covers about 2.400 persons. Who are those persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said this before, and I'll repeat. In this year, at the last meeting we had with representatives of Serbia and Montenegro an agreement was reached and documented, and it stipulates that on the territory of the Republic of Croatia, it can be considered that there are 2.400 missing persons. 500 of them are being sought by Serbia and Montenegro as citizens of Serbia and Montenegro. It was the first time that it was documented, officially recorded, that citizens of Serbia and Montenegro have gone missing in Operations Flash and Storm, and 915 of them are the responsibility of the Republic of Croatia, who will continue to look for them. And there is a remaining number of persons who about registered as imprisoned and missing. That is our approach currently. So there is a large number of persons concerning whom we are looking for answers from Serbia and Montenegro, but that is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that this information you are giving us now, these numbers, would feature in some possible agreement between the two states in a situation when the process of exhumation has not been completed yet? The victims have not been exhumed or identified?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking about this, and you have now put the question more broadly and profoundly and I'll try answer as briefly as I can. When we talk about processes of exhumation, bearing in mind the fact that on the territory of the Republic of Croatia it is possible to find some of those who are being sought by Serbia and Montenegro, some members of the Yugoslav army who were killed there and who can be found and who can be exhumed, bearing in mind the fact that there are some ethnic Serbs, citizens of Croatia where there is a vested interest of Serbia and Montenegro, and bearing in mind that Serbia and Montenegro should be represented in some exhumations, agreements have been reached and -- featuring the protocol between two states, that in exhumations in Croatia but also in Serbia and Montenegro, monitors should be present from both states together with monitors of the international community. I think that's what you asked me. Which means that in all exhumations carried out in Croatia where Serbia and Montenegro has a vested interest, we provided them with access, and we have signed an agreement accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: All this that you have just told us, does this mean that the actual number of victims and persons who are really missing has not been established yet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat. At this moment, and this operation is nearing its end and there can be no dramatic changes any more, we can take it that the number of citizens gone missing in Operations Flash and Storm, not all of them being Serbs although most of them are, although it has been shown that there are some Croats and others, the number of people gone missing in Flash and Storm is at this moment 915. This whole operation has not been completed. This number will be modified, revised upwards or downwards, through the process of identification. But it doesn't mean that all these people are dead. Those people are in the category of missing persons. As for your question about those who were killed, I said that we have submitted this information both to the international community and to the representatives of Serbia and Montenegro. But not only the information but the dossiers complete with photographs with the aim of preliminary identification. And according to our estimates - we can now even talk about estimates based on those documents - there remain about 500 persons from the period of Flash and Storm operations to be exhumed from known grave sites, and they have to be identified. And then we'll know to what extent they will share in this number of 915. As for persons who were killed in the period 1991 to 1995, that is before Flash and Storm operations, we cannot know how large that number is. We know that 1.140 people are regarded as missing in that period. We can assume most of them are dead. We cannot know or, rather, we don't know where their graves are, be it individual or mass graves, and we are conducting intensive exploration in this area and cooperating with Serbia and Montenegro in order to find these graves. I have to say that so far in this process we have found 140 grave sites containing this category of persons, and we have found 1.200 individual graves. However, 1.140 remain in the category of missing, and it is an open question where and when we will find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that the number of missing persons in Flash and Storm is 915, and that so far 499 were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And in terms of the marked burial sites, you expect the exhumation of another 500 people.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. So now when you put this together, the number of exhumed persons, that is 499, and number 500, which is our estimate, then the figure we have is about 1.000 persons who were fatalities in that period. That is what was officially made public after these operations. That's the figure that appeared in the media and that was presented to the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: If it is so, then how come it is possible that 915 is the registered number of missing persons whereas you say there is a thousand people involved?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, you have to distinguish between a missing person and a killed person. Missing persons we can find in different places. Some of them we can find alive. For example, as we did find some people the last couple of days. We have to bear in mind yet another aspect, and that is that some of these people did not necessarily have to get killed in the territory of the Republic of Croatia. That is to say that at this point this time or, rather, I at this point in time speak only about facts that I have available. These facts are always easily verifiable, especially because the work I do is absolutely transparent and in every step I insist on that, that the representatives of Serbia and Montenegro be involved as monitors but also representatives of the international community. These two institutions stand by everything I have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I put this question precisely because it is clear to me that among the missing persons there can be persons who are still alive. All missing persons need not be fatalities certainly?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: However, you told us that 915 is the number of missing persons and the number of dead should be a thousand. So the number of fatalities is larger than the number of missing persons. I'm asking you how come that is possible.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have to look at international humanitarian law on one hand and on the other hand we have to look at procedure related to missing persons, and the criteria were laid by the International Red Cross. These procedures state very clearly that a missing person a person about whom his or her family has no information whatsoever. After being registered a certain period of time has to go by, and it is only then that a person is confirmed as registered. In the case of fatalities, the situation is quite clear. If a family has information to the effect that a person got killed, then that person cannot be part of the category of missing persons, because it is well known that that person got killed, and one of the possibilities left to the family is to initiate proceedings for seeking mortal remains. Therefore, we have to distinguish between those two categories that were defined very clearly in this particular subject matter. Perhaps this will mean something to you as well: Out of 3.000 -- I'm speaking in general terms now. Out of about 3.000 identified persons we had in the period 1991 up to 1995, only 1.200 persons were persons who were registered as missing. What does that mean? That means that not all missing persons were registered as such for different reasons, because the family was disunited, because entire families were killed and there was no one to initiate proceedings or, on the other hand, for some reason the family simply did not initiate proceedings. So when talking about missing persons the criteria are very clear and very definite. And precisely at the last meeting we had with Serbia and Montenegro I insisted on this criteria and they accept as well and they are now single uniform criteria in that subject matter. That's how we managed to get this figure of 2.500 persons who went missing in the territory of Republic of Croatia, and that is the territorial principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: These 2.500 missing persons in the territory of the Republic of Croatia, what period of time does this figure refer to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1991 to 1996 or, rather, the end of the armed conflict after Operations Flash and Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Since you received information about 2.500 persons who went missing and you have this information in this intergovernmental cooperation, do you know the ethnic background of these missing people?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to now, no, because it is only now that it is being adopted as such. I have in my office the ethnic backgrounds of missing persons. Again, we can talk about estimates. We can say very clearly that out of the remaining 915 missing persons they are Serbs, ethnic Serbs, for the most part but not exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: If from 1995 until now it has been 11 years, are these persons alive or not based on the experience you've had?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I never go into such forecasts. For me, a missing person either recorded or not, and my job is to find the missing person.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the answer because Mr. Milovancevic spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let us go back to your report that speaks about 12.078 persons that were killed. In the report it says that 87 per cent of the persons killed out of these 12.078 are males; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the report it also says that 82.8 per cent of the killed persons are aged 18 to 60; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Out of 12.078 persons who were killed, it is stated that for 983 the age is unknown.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The explanation you provided pointed out the identification problem involved. Is it possible that if you have all details about a particular victim you do not include the year of birth if you have that at least?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly, but please, I have come to present information before a court of law, and I have to stand by every piece of information and every detail provided. For all these people for who I do not have complete information, they have been included in the category of unknown persons. And I have told you what the reasons are. I can stand by every name and surname that was recorded by a certain number. And where it is unknown, I do not have complete information, and I did not want to go into providing that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. I have understood what you're saying. As for ethnicity, the ethnicity of the killed persons, out of this 12.078, it is stated that 34.5 per cent of them or, rather, in numbers this is 4.176, are persons are unknown ethnic background. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. 4.176 persons did not declare themselves in ethnic terms. They did not provide this information. I pointed out at the beginning of my remarks that we as a state institution cannot and should not seek such information, because there is a law in the Republic of Croatia on confidentiality of information and such information is one's personal affair. So it is up to the person involved to say whether they want to provide that information or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question? Is this figure 4.176 or is it 4.167?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The figure, Your Honour, is 4.167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps I just misspoke. Perhaps there was a permutation of figures, so perhaps I just misread this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So you confirmed that for 4.167 persons you done not have information about their ethnic background. Can you tell us out of these 4.167 persons who got killed how many 18-year-olds were there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have information about these 4.167, how many people there were between the ages of 18 and 60 and how many were above 60?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, that is not customary. That is not regular practice to go into such categorisations. Information about ethnicity, gender, age, et cetera are provided, those that are known. Any further analysis is possible, but that kind of request has to be put forth. And then in such cases such analyses can be made, but regular practice is to publicize categories that were presented here. Now, going into further analysis of every category is possible, but not in this way and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Since this is a large number of killed persons, 4.167, for this number of persons can you tell us who were civilians and who were members of armed forces? Do you have information of that kind at least?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I already gave you the information that I have available, that my office has available, and that information is clearly presented. I said that it is possible to make any kind of analysis at a special request, but such analyses were never made, the kind that you are asking about now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you make an analysis for these 4.167 persons in respect of their place of residence? That's information that you should have. So can you say what municipality these killed persons belonged to and which villages or towns? Do you have information of that kind?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I'm repeating yet again that the analyses that we made and that are relevant were presented here. At this moment, I do not have any other analyses. Therefore, I cannot present them. I have to point out yet again that I never, ever heard of anyone asking for an analysis on that basis. An analysis can be made on the basis of all parameters, but I have never heard of anyone making analyses on the basis of these. If you needed such analyses, you could have asked for them like all others from our office, and you would have received them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Milovancevic, from the answer of the witness you can accept that outside the analysis that has been presented in court, this witness has prepared no other analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Only the basis of the questionnaire for missing persons, you explain that a dossier file was compiled for every person. So for these 4.167 persons, do you have complete files including all details?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the number you said? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I asked whether for these 4.167 persons whose ethnicity is unknown you have information or concrete dossiers for all of these persons.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I have to repeat yet again what I've already spoken about. We have to distinguish between a missing person and a killed person. For all missing persons there are dossiers. For all killed persons there aren't dossiers, because some people got killed in 1991, and immediately after their death they were identified and registered. Therefore, there are no dossiers. There are records on establishing cause of death or another document establishing death. So I repeat, there are dossiers, files, for missing persons, for all missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I quote part of your statement that among these 12.078 persons, 76, persons, I'm sorry, I don't want to make any mistakes, 12.078 among them, there were 6.780 defenders which is 60 per cent of the total number of persons killed.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the category of defender. Who are the persons included in this category?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia. I did not want to go into a precise categorisation of various units or branches. That's not my job. But all of them are all members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to a previous list of killed persons, it's Exhibit 413, the number of defenders was 7.861 who were killed. Do you remember that number?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait a minute. That's the number -- what is the total number of those killed, if you have that document? Can you help me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: There is an earlier list of persons killed, and the number of defenders was shown as 7.861. In the meantime, the number went down to 6.788, and the total number of those killed increased by 244. Can you tell me how this change occurred?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Under the law on Croatian defenders, members of civilian defence no longer enjoy the status of defenders; that is, cannot exercise rights to benefits and other rights as that category, so they were removed from the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You stated that in the job you occupied dealing with the matters that were within your purview you applied Geneva Conventions. Geneva Conventions used term "members of armed forces," and you use the term "defender." Are these terms identical?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, member of armed forces or defender. I did not introduce the term. That category was introduced under the law on Croatian defenders that was adopted in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You just said that the number of those defenders was diminished by a certain number because members of civilian defence were taken off the list of armed forces.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that. I don't see what the problem is. If a certain category under the law, the current law in the Republic of Croatia, does not belong with the armed forces, is not considered to belong to armed forces, and people from that category do not enjoy the same rights as members of armed forces, that category is deleted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In view of the subject of this trial and the allegations in the indictment that relate to about one-third of the Republic of Croatia, can you give us any information about the number of killed persons in that part of Croatia that is covered by the indictment?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is almost impossible. Why? You will know -- you will allow that Zagreb was never occupied. I hope we can agree on that. But in Zagreb, we have victims, killed persons, who are included in the list of killed persons. You will also allow that in Osijek that was never occupied, we have a thousand victims, fatalities, who were killed during the shelling. They are included in the list of killed persons, but that territory had never been occupied. We also have Sisak and many other examples that I could give you now. That is why we cannot do our analyses in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that all towns in the former Republic of Serbian Krajina and all former UNPAs we have the number of people killed? Can you give us those numbers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no such data, nor did we have occasion to obtain such data. All we were able to do is to make certain analyses. We also receive certain documentation all the time, and only when that process is completed these people will be placed on record. For instance, in the area of Vukovar, as far as I know, that's what I heard, about 400 members of the Territorial Defence and the army of Yugoslavia were killed, and their bodies were shipped away and buried in the territory of Serbia and Montenegro. Some of them were citizens of Croatia. We don't have such data, and that is precisely why we are talking to Serbia and Montenegro in order to be able to receive that data and to integrate it with our numbers. But for now we have only estimates. However, I do not wish to discuss estimates. I'm only prepared to talk about the facts we have at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. I have one question that is linked to sheet number 5 in this chapter about killed persons. That's a diagram showing the ethnicity of those killed. In the column number that is next to the column "Ethnicity," we have numbers. The total number is 12.078, as mentioned in your report. Are they exhumed and identified, these people who are categorised as killed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us just try to be clear. I'm not sure I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to reformulate. On this sheet 5, in the table dealing with the number of those killed there is indication of ethnicity. All I want to know is are these people recorded as victims, 12.078? Are all those people exhumed and identified and thus recorded as killed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We have to be clear. I told you that the process of exhumation began in 1996. Through that process, to date 3.568 people were exhumed, out of which 2.000 and something were identified.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the exact number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in the total 12.078, all identified persons who were exhumed are included. They are part of the list. And that is why the list is growing. As the number of identified bodies grows, the list of persons killed is also growing but also the number of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Now we will move to paragraph 34, page 14 of your report about missing persons, and in this paragraph 34f, you say that 1.140 people are still being sought; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that those 1.140 persons are those who are registered as missing?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To be precise, those are people whose families submitted an official request to search for a missing person to my office, the office force missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That is the request that we mentioned at the beginning of the cross-examination together with the questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A family member has filled in a questionnaire for each of these 1.140, and that is the basis for the search. And if you allow me, I'll try to make it clearer. It was a widely publicised action to gather this information, and it was conducted in Croatia but also outside in all embassies of Croatia and consular offices. So every family had the opportunity to make such a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that your office is the source of this information?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the source of the information that I'm presenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
