utterances.text: 80 per cent of missing persons are males according to the information that you provided; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that 71 per cent of those missing are between 18 and 60 years old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us to what territory does this information about missing persons apply?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. The majority of missing persons is related to earlier occupied territories, formerly occupied territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to what extent is this number, 1.140 missing persons, updated? When was the last time you revised this figure?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that it is very recent. The current figure is 1.138. So the figure I gave you is very precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Today you told us that in Flash and Storm 915 persons are registered as missing. Are these persons included in this number of 1.140 or not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've already said that this action was still under way and that we now have this mandate, and that during last month, towards the end of last month, I informed the Croatian parliament about this and that's where the number was recorded. And information about these people is compiled on same questionnaires in Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and third countries, just like in the Republic of Croatia. So the action is not completed yesterday, and the number of 915 is a provisional number. There is one more thing I have to add, that in the report that went to the parliament of the Republic of Croatia, it was stated unequivocally that in the Republic of Croatia 1.140 persons are registered as missing in Croatia, and in addition to that, another 915 missing persons in Operations Flash and Storm and that this activity of information-gathering is not finished yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This information that you provided to us, does it mean that your report is simply inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Allow me to finish my question. That in this report you just mentioned 1.140 missing persons without involving or including the 915 persons who went missing in Flash and Storm, and that was not mentioned in your written report at all.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could not have been mentioned in that way anyway in view of the situation as it is and the period when I handed in my report. In addition to that, this information related to Flash and Storm does not pertain to persons registered in our office. Therefore, I gave information, and I pointed that out several times, that those persons who handed in requests for looking for missing persons were registered as such. As for this activity concerning 915 persons, that is something completely different. This is our activity aimed at establishing the actual state of affairs. And once it is established, then the two will be brought together and this will become official.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: As for these 915 persons, apart from the list of 1.140. So these 915 persons, do you consider them to be missing persons, and do you rector them as missing persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We consider them to be missing persons, but there is a clear differentiation precisely so that this number would not be abused. That is to say the cumulative figure abused in different ways. That is to say that there is a clear differentiation among missing persons in terms of the periods of time involved. So it is called the first conflict and the second conflict. And indeed some other rules are applied as well. There is another important thing. It is important that we started the initiative to have our questionnaires applied, that these persons were recorded and that these records contributed to the identification of missing persons, and that is a very clear position that the lists will be brought together once this action is completed. There is one more thing I have to add which is very important, that in every one of these requests families were asked for their consent in order to have this information provided to our office. It's a very complex matter therefore, because it is the family that submits this request. We as an institution cannot force anyone to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 14 in 34f, you wrote that in view of the year when they went missing, 943 persons went missing in 1991. 13 persons went missing in 1992. 15 persons went missing in 1993,3 persons went missing in 1994, and 22 persons went missing in 1995. As for 44 persons, the time when they went missing is unknown, and the total is 1.140. Is that what your report says?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's what my report says, and all of these persons were recorded in that way. They filled out a form and they were registered as missing persons by our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: However, this figure that you provided here of 1.140 is not correct. At this moment the figure is 2.055, including the 915. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, please. I'm trying to say something for the umpteenth time, something that is very important, that persons are recorded on the basis of the family reporting the matter. In my office, 1.140 persons are recorded, and every one of these requests is signed by the party that is filing the request, and then there is an appropriate number that is filed as well. I repeat once again that knowing that a certain number of citizens of the Republic of Croatia, primarily of Serb ethnicity, went missing in Operations Flash and Storm, and seeing that there are no requests for such tracing procedures, we as an institution and I personally started a certain activity with the representatives of Serbia and Montenegro and with international representatives including the ICRC in order to find out what this figure is so that we could gather this information in a uniform manner. This action has not been completed yet. I repeat once again, as an institution we had to ask each and every family for their consent to have this information provided to our office, but the information is gathered in other states. Since this action has not been completed yesterday and it is not that our office initiated the procedure, I can only talk about this number and say that we are gathering documentation, and once this documentation is complete then all of those who gave their consent to have their information taken will be included in the joint list. We have a joint list, but these people did not file requests. I do not have official requests filed, and I can only talk about those for whom an official request was filed, and that figure is 1.140, and that is the basis for all of these analyses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us from what moment you knew of this number of persons, 915, apart from the 1.140?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The action started in the year 2000, and the action is still under way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That will do. Thank you. Please, in the report that you sent to the Court, you said that 22 persons went missing in 1995. Let me just finish this. Let me finish my question. Can you explain to us why you did not write this what you are telling us now in order to present such facts?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, your opposite number, Mr. Milovancevic. Yes, Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think my opposite member is going around and around in circles on the same issue which has been asked and answered multiple times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any answer to that, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to get answer from the witness about the moment from which he knew of these 915 missing persons, and the answer I got was from the year 2000. I don't need anything else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me. I did not give that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, do you have any response to make to the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since today is the first time that we received a series of information from the witness, 332 bodies, 915 missing people, and so on, various things that are not contained in the report, I'm just trying to correlate this to the information provided in the written report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, Mr. Milovancevic. Mr. Milovancevic, do you accept that you are going round and round in circles, or do you not accept? And if you do not accept, why do you not accept?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm no longer going to insist on these matters. I withdraw my last question in order to move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. I will uphold the objection. You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, let us move on to expelled persons. That is page 11, 34a. These figures pertain to displaced persons, if I understand this correctly, and they do not come from your office but from the office for displaced persons for -- of another ministry, for trade, tourism, maritime affairs, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Administration for Displaced Persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Don't you find this strange that the Ministry for Sea and Tourism through its administration deals with displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not for me to say what I think about the establishment of the state that was set up in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you, Mr. Grujic. My next question has to do with the figure of 220.338 persons that you refer to as displaced, and as you say, "in the aggression against the Republic of Croatia." Can you tell us what period and what territory this information refers to, this information about displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the total number of recorded displaced persons recorded in the administration for displaced persons. And every displaced person has a file of his own, and I think they have been provided in the attachment. So that is the total number of displaced persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us about this total number of refugees, whether it includes persons of Serb ethnicity who were displaced, expelled to the territory of Serbia also after Operation Flash and Storm?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We have to put things right in that respect too. Yes. Now, what is this about? First and foremost, it is a question of terminology. We have to distinguish between displaced persons and refugees and expellees. Your question yesterday was precisely aim at that. I now avail myself of this opportunity, because I did not say it yesterday, that there should and proper distinction in terms of this terminology. In keeping with this terminology that is used in this field, I gave information about displaced persons because that's the information that I was asked to provide. According to this information, it was stated very clearly that 20 -- 220.338 people were recorded as displaced persons, an ethnic composition of them was provided, saying 205.215 were ethnic Croats, 4.987 of Serb ethnicity, 3.104 Hungarians, whereas there are others as well. So when talking about displaced persons, that is the category I spoke of arranges I gave the exact number too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think the numbers now got confused. Maybe it's a problem of translation, but could you repeat that out of the 205.215 were ethnic Croats, Serbs, and so on? It seems to be wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is the information: 220.338 persons were registered in the category of displaced persons. As for their ethnic affiliation, there are 205.215 persons of Croat ethnicity, then there is 4.987 persons of Serb ethnicity, 3.104 persons that are Hungarians, and 7.032 persons that are of other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: 34b -- no, 34a, this table speaks of Hungarians 4.987, and Serbs 3.104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you hear that, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I'm trying to check. I'm sorry. I inversed the numbers. I inversed the figures for Serbs and Hungarians inadvertently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What does that mean? Does it mean the Hungarians are 4.987, and the Serbs are 3.104? That's the correct -- okay. You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember getting an answer to my earlier question, so I'll repeat it. Can you tell us to what period this number applies, 220.328 expelled persons, and to what territory?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think the question was put using the term expelled persons, and the witness has already mentioned, not just today but in the report, that this analysis pertains to displaced persons and that there are distinctions between these terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you hear that, Mr. Milovancevic? There's a distinction between "displaced" and "expelled" terms in the terminology of the witness. Maybe if you put your question again in the correct terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I heard what my colleague from the Prosecution said. I quoted from the B/C/S, page 11, 34a of the expert report, and it says just before the table that in the aggression against the republic of Croatia, 220.338 people were expelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have an answer to that, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat, Your Honour. We have to distinguish between expelled persons, displaced persons, and refugees. Those are the three terms used for this population. According to the information available to me, and I have stated it, it's 220.338 people expelled for the entire period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Expelled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Expelled, the driven out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Milovancevic, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Court is adjourned and will come back at half past twelve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. Milovancevic, I just want to get clarity from Mr. Grujic on a few things here. Mr. Grujic, what do you say for "displaced person"? I'm going ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you get my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. So in Croatia, the term "displaced person" is used specifically for Croatia where people left their homes for different reasons and moved to another locality within the state, which means that we had situations where people were displaced from one area to another area within Croatia. So that is when we use the term "displaced person." Then there is the term "refugee." Those, in our terminology, are people who left their homes and went to other states, where they received the status of refugees, which involves certain benefits and assistance. Expellees are persons who are forcibly driven out from their homes and have the status of expellees in the Republic of Croatia. So we have those three categories. And I provided my data related to expellees as I was asked to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, am I right to say that the distinction between "displaced" and "expelled" is that an expelled person is expelled through human action, whereas displaced may not necessarily be through human action? For instance, people could be displaced by floods. Is that the distinction between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the most part, Your Honour, yes. Displaced persons can be displaced for a variety of reasons, to avoid conscription, for instance, or to find better quality of life, or out of fear from possible war or any other pressure. So reasons for displacement can vary. And we have about 35.000 people on record, official record, as displaced. But I did not cover them in my report. I covered in my report exclusively expelled persons, people who left their homes because they were forced to under pressure, coercion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I would like you to comment on is the pressure that is put on expellees is pressure put on by human action. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is so. Exclusively human pressure. Fear for one's own life or because one simply has to leave under threat of force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Grujic. Mr. Milovancevic, those are the distinctions that the witness gives between those words, and I hope that any confusion that we may have had will be eliminated now. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, these details found in 34a of your report, page 11 of B/C/S, where we see that in the aggression against the Republic of Croatia, 220.338 persons were expelled, that relates to which period? I mean years.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me correct you. You didn't give the correct number. It's 220.338. And if you look at table number 7, you will see the various periods, precise periods, with exact indication with the number of expellees recorded for each period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My question was very specific, Mr. Grujic. Does this number you mention relate to the period 1991/1995 or not? You name the period.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As indicated in the table, from 1991 until -- it says the last category was recorded from the 6th of August, 1995, onwards. That's the last category on record. So it starts with -- it starts with 1991, where 186.903 were recorded until the 2nd of May --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. We cannot go on with these figures so fast. We have to see the document on the ELMO or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you just hold on, Mr. Grujic. The interpreters say they cannot go on with these figures unless they see them somewhere written. Can we put them on the monitor for the interpreters, please? My immediate question to you, Mr. Grujic, is that you've just told us that -- or, rather, the question put to you is expelled people, 220.338. This table doesn't talk of expelled people, it talks of displaced people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's probably a mistranslation. So this table is about expelled persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, you have told us that you viewed data until the 6th of August, 1995, if I understood you correctly. When does that period start in 1991, because we can't see it from the table.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. You can't see it from the table because the statistics kept by that office was done by these periods, but it is clear and well known that the first deportations started in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can we then note your answer as being that this figure about expelled persons applies to the period from August 1991 until the 6th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can repeat. What is explicitly written here, and I stated it in my testimony, the statistics is presented in this table by periods relevant to the office that keeps these records. From 1991 until 1992, we have the figure of 186.903 expelled persons. That's 1991 to 1992. I don't have the exact initial date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Before you go on, Mr. Milovancevic, I'd like to ask the witness about what is on the last line of this graph where there's the asterisk beginning "Information," and ending with the digit 9. There is obviously digit missing. What should that digit be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I don't have that in my report, and the translation -- would somebody be able to assist me maybe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try and assist you. There is an asterisk at the bottom of that table which explains the table, and it says, "Information from August 6, 1995 concerns displaced persons who have returned from other countries but have been treated as displaced persons since 19," and then there is "9," and we want to know 1990 what. That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 199. That is what is written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what is written. It's obviously a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 199. Maybe I can try to explain. The thing is that the list includes 199 persons who are outside the Republic of Croatia and later returned. So they had been expelled to somewhere outside Croatia and then returned. Let me try to be specific. There were cases where people were expelled from their homes and couldn't find quarter in the Republic of Croatia, and some countries received them as refugees, and after a short while they returned to their country and continued in their status of expelled persons within this category. I don't know if my explanation is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is not clear. I'll tell you why it is not clear. That figure 199 is preceded by the word "since," so 199 must refer to time, not to a number of people. It relates to time. These people have been displaced since some year, 1990 something. There must be a digit after the last 9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's probably 1991, but I really cannot say with any certainty because on my copy I don't have this number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Wouldn't your records help you in any way to determine the precise year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try, although I'm not quite sure if I'll succeed. But it seems unbelievable that we could have two different figures.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I in the interim point something out? I have the B/C/S version here of page 7, and I see that the -- the top row where dates are is not in the English. Perhaps those dates are on page 8 of the English, but as it currently stands, page 7 of the English doesn't contain the top row, which is on page 7 of the B/C/S. And the last line on the English version is not in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then can we either get the top row of the English version so that we can see the period? Yes, can we get that either on page 8 or page 6? If it is on the top row, it should be at page 6 and not at page 8. This is page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think that in the chart on page 7, the dates have been left out in the English version. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are the dates available in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And can that version be given to the witness so that he can read those dates and they can be interpreted for us and we can get them on the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Ms. Valabhji, I wanted to find out, does it mean then that where the asterisk starts from "Information" to "199," that should be removed from this graph? You said it don't exist in the B/C/S version, if I understood you properly. It does not relate to this in any way?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. On the English version, that line "Information from," and so on, is not in the B/C/S. My senior counsel has noticed that the asterisk is there in the B/C/S version. The asterisk corresponds to the 6th of August, 1995, but there is no corresponding explanation next to the asterisk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Do we know how that information got there then?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, these charts were -- perhaps the witness could explain about the asterisk. These charts were actually provided to us by the witness, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe he should answer. But are we able to put on the monitor the first row that shows dates? Now, Mr. Grujic, for purposes of the transcript, we are going to ask you to read that first row of that chart that is in B/C/S so that we know from when it starts. It looks like it starts from the 1st of May, 1992, going up to the 6th of August, 1995, but it's for you to read it and tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This table was developed on the basis of available data, and it depicts the number of persons expelled by periods -- by periods that were specified by the office for expelled persons. That is in the way that they found it possible to process statistically. And at the same time, it deals with each county, each territorial unit from which these people were expelled. So the breakdown is by county and by period. The first period is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. We just want the dates. We are aware of all that breakdown. Just give us the dates from when this operation started and when it ended.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the first date mentioned is until the 1st of May, 1992, which means the first five months of 1992 and 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you translate for us the heading above all these lines, "Razdoblje Progonstva," and then it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Period of expulsion." That's the first line. Below that we have the second line that starts with "County," that's the territorial unit. Below that we have a list of counties from which people were expelled. Horizontally -- and the next line is the period for which these expelled people were recorded, and the first column is until the 1st of May, 1992. So they did not state the initial date. But it is clear it covers 1991 and the first five months of 1992. From then onwards we have all dates specified, from the 2nd of May, 1992, until the 31st of December, 1992. Then from the 1st of January, 1993, until the 31st of December, 1993. And on, from the 1st of January, 1994, until the 31st of December, 1994. The following column is from the 1st of January, 1995, until the 8th of August, 1995. And the last column is from the 6th of August, 1995 onwards. So it's open-ended. It was done in this way because the statistical information is as it is, and those were the possibilities they had for presenting this data. Of course it would have been much better to quote the date when the first case was recorded but that's how these records are kept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: There seems to be a mistake concerning this line, 1st of January, 1995 to 8th of August. Doesn't it have to be until 5th of August? Otherwise, these -- this and the next one would overlap. And then the last line we didn't get in translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do not take into account the last line, because obviously there was a computer mistake when the CDs were being recorded. So that's why it's not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What does the last line say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot read it. I cannot read what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Broj --"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not shown now. What we see on the monitors is not -- does not include that. But the English version does show it. The table that we're looking at now is all right though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, what we would like to understand is the last column next to the column dated the 6th of August, 1995. To the right of that, what is that heading, the one which ends -- I'm sorry -- if you can bring it more to the left. No, no, no, it's -- more to the left. More. That last column, that column. That column. And that has "Broj Rodjenih u Progonstvu."

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Evidently we have a mistake here, a typo. It is a purely technical error. It says from the 8th of August, 1995, and then it should say the 8th of 8th, 1995. So instead of the 6th of August, 1995, it should say the 8th of August, 1995 onwards. It's obviously a technical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. The next column, Mr. Grujic, after that column that you've been talking about, what does it talk about, the one whose total at the bottom is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the next column refers to the number of children born in exile, which means that their parents were expelled and that these children were born in exile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, can you tell us how many expellees refer to what you call the occupied territory of the Republic of Croatia and what I call the Republic of the Serb Krajina? So how many expellees come from the territory that was the UNPAs, the UN protected areas?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We have to clarify some of these matters. All these people come from that area. All these people lived in that area, and they were expelled from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that this number of 220.338 persons is the number of people who were expelled from the territory of one-third of Republic of Croatia that this indictment refers to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question correctly, Mr. Milovancevic, as you can see, according to the information depicted here, all these people, if we're talking about expellees as we are, were expelled precisely from the territories that were occupied, one-third of the territory that was occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of statistical figures from the census pertaining to 1991 about the number of Croats in the territory of the SAO Krajina and later the Republic of Serb Krajina or, as you say, the occupied territories?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of the ethnic composition. I can talk about the ethnic composition on the basis of the census made in 1991, and that's the information I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many inhabitants of Croat ethnicity lived in that one-third of the territory that is being discussed here?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you for a bit of time because it's not related directly to my testimony, but I'll try to give an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone and speak up a bit, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, when you speak please speak into the microphone. And, Mr. Milovancevic, what year does your question relate to? Your question is, "Can you tell us how many inhabitants of Croat ethnicity lived in that one-third of the territory that is being discussed here." In what year, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at the beginning of my question, which was in the previous question, I mentioned 1991 and the census that defined this number, which should be an undisputed figure between the Defence and the Prosecution, as far as this is concerned, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please finish your question anyway. The witness is answering the question that you put, not the previous one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give me a moment to try to find something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have all the time, Mr. Grujic. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, regarding the question concerning the census, it would be helpful if the Defence were to point out which areas are being referred to, because in 1991 there were a lot of changes in the area, and it's not clear exactly what geographic area is being referred to by the 1991 census cited by my opponent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My reading of the question certainly refers to the entire area that was occupied. Now, I don't know whether there is a census for all that entire area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think this area there are fluctuations in terms of this area in the picture in 1991. I don't think that it's -- the boundaries or the lines are set, and it remained the same way throughout 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let the witness tell us what he finds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can now give some tentative information for starters if this will be satisfactory for the Defence attorney. The Defence counsel asked me about what territory this pertained to. I can say that at the beginning of 1992, 1.074 settlements were occupied. Permanently populated ones, that is. From 1.074 occupied settlements, Croats constituted a majority in 364 of these settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Distinguished Mr. Grujic, I did not ask you what you said just now. The Prosecutor in the indictment refers to a certain number of expelled persons. That number is linked up to statistics concerning ethnic Croats who as citizens of Croatia lived in the territory of the Republic of the Serb Krajina up to 1991 and in 1991. I am asking you whether you know how many inhabitants of Croat ethnicity lived there at the time. And if you don't know that, you can tell us now that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very hard to answer your question. Why? Because the set-up was different territorially, administratively in 1991 compared to the present-day situation when we have the establishment according to counties. We would now have to look at each and every municipality individually and to see which one was in the temporarily occupied areas, and, of course, I cannot tell you that right now. So your question is such that it is basically impossible to answer it, because now we have an administrative set-up that is different, and I cannot tell you exactly the borders and what the exact composition of the population was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Lest there be any misunderstanding as to what the occupied areas is or whether it is occupied or not, in the Vance Plan according to which UN troops were deployed in Croatian territory, territory of the Republic of Croatia at that time, the exact municipalities were listed, those that existed at that time in 1991 and the beginning of 1992 that are part of the UNPAs, the UN protected areas. Those are the areas I'm referring to. However, since you cannot give me any information in respect of these municipalities, my next question is as follows: On map 6 -- or, rather, on page 6 of your report, which pertains to expelled persons according to counties, that's what it says in B/C/S, you mentioned counties as a form of a territorial organisation, the present-day territorial organisation as the Republic of Croatia as it stands today. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Here there is a territorial distribution and information related to that, and that is what was provided in the previous table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to display on the monitor this map of displaced persons according to counties so the gist of my question would be understood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. I didn't turn on my microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, on this map of Croatia we see the counties that you later refer to in this vertical table; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On this map you can see that an entire series of counties has access to the Adriatic Sea all along, Splitsko-Dalmatinska, Sibenska-Zadarska, Licko-Senjska are the ones. Let's just restrict ourselves to that.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: It is obvious that the territory of the counties for which you developed these figures is much bigger than what the territory of the Republika Srpska Krajina was. Do you agree with that assertion?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not agree with your assertion, because we can go from one county to another, and in every county there were activities that were aimed at expelling people, starting from Dobrovacko, Nejokansko [phoen], Splitsko, Dalmatinska, and so on and so forth. We can move from one town to another, from one village to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That was into the my question, Mr. Grujic. Please follow my question very carefully. My question was about the number of expelled persons from the territory of the Republic of Srpska Krajina, not from the territory of the present-day counties which are a new form of territorial organisation. Can you give us this information that we are interested in, the number of expellees from the territory of the Republic of Srpska Krajina or the UN protected areas?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot, because things are being put differently now. You have now put it completely differently. We have a valid territorial principle which was presented as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Mr. Grujic. Let's not dwell on this any longer, not to keep the Trial Chamber. You came here to testify as an expert and also to give answers pertaining to the territory that is mentioned in the indictment, a territory that is different from the territory that you depict on this map. It differs by one-third, and now you're telling me you don't have information about this territory; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not right. Could your questions please be formulated clearly. I assert here and I state explicitly we have a territorial principle that is in force now, and I repeat that each and every one of these mentioned counties had activities on its territory that led to the expulsion of people. Now, you are going to different dates, not 1991, not 1995, not 2000, but you're talking about when some plan was elaborated. I claim as an expert that these people were expelled - expelled - from their houses, from their homes by way of activities that were gathered towards their expulsion and that all these counties, therefore, were linked to activities pertaining to armed conflict in the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, can I just ask -- can I just understand your question? How does this area differ with the area that was, as you call it, the SAO Krajina? Is it from the names?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the territory of SAO Krajina, or the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina, the Prosecution uses this term "so-called," represents only one-third of this territory that you see on the map, and I'm asking this expert now whether he's able to tell us. From that territories which was allegedly or really under the control of Serbian Krajina, he knows how many were expelled, not from the entire territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in this area is represented by the SAO Krajina? Just tell us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely why I asked the witness this question, because in the meantime the administrative organisation has been changed and the expert is speaking to the latest administrative division regardless of the fact that it is quite different in the maps and atlases we have been using as exhibits. So I'm asking him now about the number of expelled from UNPAs, for instance, and he answers me that he was looking also at other areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's telling you that he's dealing with this -- these areas that are shown on the map, which are listed on this table. You say that this area occupies more than a third of -- no. You're saying that the area that you call SAO Krajina is only a third of what is shown here, and I'm saying which is that third, because obviously he doesn't seem to understand what you're talking about. What is that third which constitutes the SAO Krajina here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't think it's my job to explain this. That's what I'm trying to elicit from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Explain your question to the witness so that the witness understands what you're asking. You are saying to him, "You can't give me this whole map because the SAO Krajina only constitutes a third of this map." Now, he doesn't know which is that third that you're talking about. And put the third to him, let him dispute it or confirm it. Put that third that you say constitutes the SAO Krajina to him. If you don't put it to him, how is he to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand your point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this map that we see on the monitor, do we see the map of the area of Croatia where UN troops called UNPROFOR arrived?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This map does not show the borders of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. That's all I wanted. Let us move on. The towns that we see on this map, Split, Sibenik, Zadar, were they in the territory of the Serbian Krajina ever?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we see here are not towns but counties. And let me try to clarify this, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let me just go through my questions. All these counties that we see on the monitor now, were they an integral part of the then Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parts of those counties were occupied, and that's what I said before. And precisely from the occupied parts those people we have seen in tables were expelled, from the occupied parts of these counties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let me ask you one thing. Can you tell us so that we can more easily visualise it, which part of what we see on the monitor was under UNPAs?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can show roughly, but people were expelled even before UNPAs were established. In Osijek Baranja county, this upper part was occupied. It's called Baranja. And part of the Osijek county also stretches towards the Vukovar-Srem county. From that area, 36.660 people were expelled. The Vukovar-Srem county was partly occupied, this area I'm showing now. That is, more than half of the county was occupied. From that area, from the Vukovar-Srem county, 55.644 persons were expelled. Part of the Virovitica-Srem, and Bilogora county, as well as the Pozega-Srem county belonged to sector west, and this area, let me draw a line here, this area approximately was occupied in those three counties, and you can see the numbers of expelled persons on the table. The Sisak-Moslavina county was occupied in this part, towards Bosnia all the way up to Sisak, and 32.865 persons were expelled. The Karlovac county was occupied from Slunj almost from Karlovac towards the Lika-Senj county. So this here was occupied. The Zadar county, including the towns of Benkovac and others, this part that I'm showing was under occupation. The Sibenik-Knin county, again this part leaning on Zadar was occupied, and partly the area of Split-Dalmatia county. The Dubrovnik county was also subject to shelling and other means of coercion, so it was occupied partly, and 6.270 people were expelled from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that means all these figures related to expelled persons, these 220.338, relates to those areas that were the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina under the control of the accused here according to the allegations of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the Dubrovnik-Neretva county. I'm not sure whether it was under their control or not, but the rest certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This figure you stated, does it mean that in other parts of those counties no single person was expelled from other parts of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat this again. That's the number of persons who were recorded as expelled persons by the office for expelled persons, and they were recorded as such by the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us -- thank you, usher. I will not need your help any more. In view of the moment when your office was established and the moment from which you have been doing this work, who determined the status of these persons, whether they were displaced, refugees, or expelled in 1991 and partly 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the job of my office ever. I have this information because I need it for my negotiations with Serbia and Montenegro, because they have their own commission for humanitarian affairs and missing persons, and because of that I have to have these figures in my office. But I get from other institutions in order to be able to do my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So these figures reflecting the number of expelled persons was given to you by other services, other institutions. You just processed them.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I processed them. But this is an official number that was published in official publications.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement or, rather, in the background material that the Prosecution submitted to us on the 15th of March this year regarding you as a witness, it is written that as a witness you mentioned in your interview with the Prosecution the following numbers are estimates regarding displaced persons from 1991 to 1995, that around 300.000 persons, mainly Serbs, left their homes in Croatia and that outside of that those who remained in Croatia are estimated at 50.000 or so. Did you give these numbers to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. We have now come precisely to the point we've been discussing today and yesterday, the various categories of people who left their homes. Here when you spoke about estimates, those estimates come from a variety of sources, and they vary from 200 to 300.000 persons who were refugeed in 1995 after Operations Flash and Storm. So they are refugees, not expellees, and they have the status of refugees in other states. 35.000 persons were displaced. That means that from some areas in Croatia such as Western Slavonia, they moved to, let's say, the Vukovar-Srem county where they resettled and were recorded. So it's a fluctuation of population caused by a variety of reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to finish. When we talk about refugees, and if we said we have an estimate of around 300.000 people refugeed after Operations Flash and Storm, then we have to mention in the same breath that dealing with the category of refugees that we haven't been doing so far, we have to say that in the Republic of Croatia, apart from those expelled persons we discussed, 402.768 persons were recorded as refugees from Bosnia, as well as 10.407 persons recorded as refugees from Serbia and Montenegro. When we talk about estimates, we have an estimate of around 300.000. I don't want to discuss estimates. I can only talk about facts. So at this point we can assert that 120.323 persons left Croatia as refugees and later returned, and new -- newly returned persons are another 10.000 or so. I can say that 120.323 persons returned to Croatia after being refugeed. There can be more, but then I would have to go into the area of estimates, and I don't want to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: According to this material disclosed to us by the Prosecution, you said that around 300.000 persons, mainly Serbs, left their homes during Operations Flash and Storm. You called them refugees, and you said that outside that number it is estimated that another 50.000 remained in the Republic of Croatia. 50.000 of whom?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is estimated that 50.000 people left, let's say Western Slavonia or Lika, and resettled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: My opponent has said that according to the material disclosed to us by the Prosecution, around 300.000 persons, mainly Serbs, left their homes during Flash and Storm. I think that misstates the material disclosed, and according to my information, the material says that the witness mentioned the following figures which are estimates in relation to displaced persons, 1991, to 1995, about 300.000 persons, mostly of Serbian ethnicity left their homes in Croatia. Out of these, an estimated 50.000 stayed on the territory of Croatia and about 120.000 returned to their homes. I don't see a mention of Flash and Storm in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, there is no mention of Flash and Storm according to Ms. Valabhji, and how do you bring in Flash and Storm? And while you are on your feet, is Flash and Storm the case we are dealing with?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I put this number to the witness from the material given us by the Prosecution, and it was all precisely as stated by my learned friend just now. Since the witness has already replied that this estimate of around 300.000 people who left Croatia is related to Operations Flash and Storm, I just continued the same line of questioning trying to get to the gist. If I was going about it clumsily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are going about it clumsily, I'm afraid, Mr. Milovancevic. If in the material supplied by your opponent there is no reference to Flash and Storm, then you have no right to include a reference to Flash and Storm unless you say, My learned friend you are wrong. You should have included Flash and Storm and I'm going to include it for the following reasons. When you just drop Flash and Storm with those figures of 300.000 and 50.000, you are bringing in, one, a completely different era, and two a complete little different event from what has been put to you by the Prosecution. But if that is your case, make it clear that that is your case. Don't attribute that to the Prosecution or to the witness. Say, "It is my case as the Defence that these figures have got to do with Flash and Storm." Don't impute them to other people when they are not either their testimony or their allegations. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, a moment ago I put to you this report from the Prosecution that mentions 300.000 persons, mainly Serbs, who left their homes in Croatia, and outside of that number another 50.000 that remained in the territory of Croatia. Those numbers are contained in the report of the Prosecution sent to the Defence on the 15th of March, 2006. When I mentioned this, you answered, and it is on record, I hope, that these numbers given us by the Prosecution do relate to Operations Flash and Storm. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This move of the population that was named refugees occurred after Operations Flash and Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My colleague from the Prosecution in her objection used the term "displaced persons," unlike the term that you are using. She spoke about 300.000 persons, approximately, of displaced persons. So what are they exactly? Are they refugees or displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's a misinterpretation or mistranslation, but I said expressly that those people are refugees. They are on record as refugees. They have refugee IDs which allow them to reside in the territories of states where they are refugees. But this is, I have to repeat again, an estimate. We don't have a solid figure. The solid figure is 120.000 people who returned. It is also certain that around 50.000 people remained in Croatia but are displaced, because from one place in one state they moved to another place in the same state. That's what we call displaced. 35.000 of them are to be found in the Vukovar-Srem county.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of this figure, around 300.000 people that you call displaced, do you know where they went after the Operations Flash and Storm?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, those are estimates, and I know that part of these people are currently as refugees in Serbia and Montenegro, or at least were. Part of them are in Bosnia. Also, they went to third countries. So that is what I know. However, I do not have any official data as to how many such persons are where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that out of these about 300.000 part of them went to Serbia and Montenegro and some to Bosnia and others abroad. Does that mean that none of these 300.000 people remained in Croatia after that operation? I mean, these 300.000.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are different estimates involved, stating about 300.000 persons who left their homes. The most realistic estimate is that in this -- these 300.000 there are also the persons who are called displaced persons, that they are also included in that figure. However, you see these are forecasts, and I don't want to stand by that. And they come from different sources, and they are all more or less the same. All sources say between 250.000 and 300.000. But I can talk about 120.323 persons who had fled and who returned now. They are recorded as such, and that is the figure that we can talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for telling us.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can also give the structure too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Just a brief question before we finish the cross-examination for today.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that the estimate was that after all of this, in the territory of the Republic of Croatia there was about 50.000 people. Are you trying to say that after Operations Flash and Storm in the territory of Croatia there was a total of about 50.000 persons of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. Again, I have to be very accurate, very precise. I really do not understand this kind of question. Please take a look at the current census and you will see how many Serbs still live in the Republic of Croatia. These are 300.000. This is a prognosis stating that 300.000 left their homes and got the status of refugees, and these people include those 50.000 who just changed their place of residence within the Republic of Croatia, which is not to say that in those areas where these 300.000 had fled from there is not a large number of people left there of Serb ethnicity and other refugees, because these areas had been populated, were populated and remain populated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that we have overstepped our time for about two or three minutes already, so I suggest that we conclude for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. That brings us to the end of the trial today. We will come back tomorrow in Courtroom II at 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of April, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
